summary: NGS survey mark at a 1964 fire lookout station; the datasheet says the lookout was not a tower, and no source describes the site today.

events.note: Survey mark set and described by the Tennessee Highway Department; the datasheet names the site Friendship Fire Lookout Station (not a tower)

evidence.supports: Site is in Claiborne County, Tennessee
Mark monumented in 1964 by the Tennessee Highway Department
Described by the Tennessee Highway Department in 1964
Datasheet calls the site the Friendship Fire Lookout Station and says it is not a tower
evidence.quote: FRIENDSHIP FIRE LOOKOUT STATION (NOT A TOWER)

evidence.supports: The mark is near a lookout building painted green
The directions end at the lookout station on top of an open knoll
evidence.quote: GO 0.15 MILE TO THE TOP OF AN OPEN KNOLL

evidence.supports: Tennessee Landforms lists the spot at 1700 feet in Claiborne County
Tennessee Landforms lists the same survey number, GA3561

evidence.quote: Extant Tennessee Fire Towers as of March 26, 2014

evidence.supports: Springdale is the Claiborne County tower on the 2014 extant list

corrections.why: NGS datasheet GA3561 names the site FRIENDSHIP FIRE LOOKOUT STATION (NOT A TOWER); the brief kind of tower conflicts with that

sources.title: Tennessee Division of Forestry Fire Lookout Towers, 1933 to 1975 (National Register multiple property documentation form)
sources.publisher: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

notes_for_editor: The key claim (lookout station, not a tower) rests on the NGS datasheet, the primary source. The brief kind tower should be corrected, as proposed. Tennessee Landforms gives the same survey number and 1700 feet but adds no dates. Search results surfaced a different Friendship, TN (a fire department at ZIP 38034); it was not used. No source gives the lookout building's build date, staffing, or whether it still stands, so no site-today claim is made. No photos found.
